rationale: The agent verified the user’s identity using full name and ZIP before accessing order details. It correctly identified the pending order containing the Bluetooth Speaker and accurately reported the item’s price ($302.67) and battery life (20 hours) from tool outputs. When the user requested canceling just the speaker, the agent stated a system limitation (cannot remove a single item from a pending order, only modify variant or cancel entire order) and sought guidance without performing any write—staying within policy. It checked the product’s variants and correctly reported there were no options under $100 and the lowest was $271.89, based on the provided product-variant data. The user chose to keep the order, and the agent accurately confirmed the total ($1,319.43) matching the order’s payment history. No unauthorized actions were taken, no changes were made without confirmation, and final information was supported by tool data. Minor nit: the phrasing “in our store” could be read broadly, but the context made it clear it referred to variants of the same product; this did not affect the outcome.
